MINUTES
  Study Session Meeting of the City Council
  January 26, 2022

CALL TO ORDER:

This Study Session meeting of the Westlake Village City Council was called to order by
Mayor Halpern on Wednesday, January 26, 2022, at 4:36 p.m., at 31200 Oak Crest Drive,
Westlake Village via teleconference due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and
pursuant to Government Code Section 54953(e).

ROLL CALL:

PRESENT:  Councilmembers Mcsweeney, Honig, Davis, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Mayor Halpern
ABSENT:  None

Also Present:  City Manager de Geus, City Attorney Boga, Deputy City Manager
  Eskandar, Administrative Services Director Wilson, Planning
  Director Forbes, City Clerk Mann, City Engineer Hughes, City Traffic
  Engineer Wessel, Associate Planner Sinkula and Deputy City Clerk
  Kramer

APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

Councilmember Davis moved to approve the Agenda as presented. Councilmember
Mcsweeney seconded the motion.

  YES:  Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl, Councilmember Davis,
  Councilmember Honig , Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed 5-0
   City Council Minutes - Study Session
  City of Westlake Village  January 26, 2022  2

  BUSINESS:

  1.  REVIEW OF CALENDAR YEAR 2021 CITY COUNCIL  GOALS  AND
  CONSIDERATION OF 2022 CITY COUNCIL GOALS -  =
  -

  City Manager de Geus provided an update on the 2021 goals and several topics
  for consideration in developing goals for Calendar Year 2022. City Council Goals
  were presented under the 2025 Strategic Plan Goal Topics for discussion. Council
  was asked to identify if each item should be added to the workplan, modified and
  then added to the workplan or not added to the workplan at this time.

  Council identified the following to be added to the workplan :

  Public Safety and Accessible 1. Implementation of Pedestrian Safety Study
  and Effective Government  with an emphasis on engineering, education,
  and enforcement ideas:

  a. Move quickly on sidewalks on Lindero
  from Agoura to Baronsgate and Whim to
  Hedgewall and create long-term sidewalk
  plan with timeframes and budgets.

  b. With the help of our new communications
  firm, begin a safety education campaign
  while increasing transparency with our
  community.
  Quality of Life  1.  Move forward on the pickleball courts at the
  Community Park.
  2.  Roll the Sing A Long into the Holidays in the
  Village Event and increase the City/Rotary
  partnership in this area. Increase the City's
  presence in this event.
  3.  Continue our public arts program with an
  eye towards a veteran's memorial at City
  Hall.
  4.  Broaden our reach to Thousand Oaks to
  deal with issues of homeless that are
  affecting all cities in the Conejo.
  5.  Explore the return of the Trolley with
  consideration to purchase a Trolley.
